preserved_objections.basis: The proposed thermal management system using a phase change material may not be effective in regulating the temperature of the battery cell during fast charging, as the study [doi:10.1109/acpee56931.2023.10135597] on fast charging method of lithium titanate battery does not provide sufficient evidence to support the use of phase change materials for thermal management in lithium-ion batteries.

The proposed system does not account for the high-temperature environment of the electric-bus depot, where the battery pack is exposed to temperatures above 40°C for extended periods, which can lead to lithium plating on the anode even with the thermal management system in place.

The study [doi:10.54337/aau681516574] on aging mechanisms in lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols contradicts the proposed solution, as it shows that lithium plating on the anode can occur even with real-time EIS monitoring and adjustment of charging parameters.

The proposed system is equivalent to the baseline, as the thermal management system and real-time EIS monitoring system do not provide any significant improvement over the current implementation, which does not use these features.
